author: LUKE THOMPSON Yakima Herald-Republic
title: West Valley's Callie Orcutt, Eisenhower's Kian Compton win district titles | CBBN | yakimaherald.com
text:
The finishes to Thursday's varsity races at the District 5 championships on Franklin Park's three-mile course couldn't have looked more different.
West Valley sophomore Callie Orcutt cruised to her second straight individual title, crossing the finish line in 18 minutes, 32 seconds before anyone else even turned the corner onto the last straightaway. Eisenhower sophomore Kian Compton needed to work much harder to complete back-to-back district titles, catching Eastmont's Cade Hill and barely hanging on to win by four-tenths of a second in 15:25, leading the Cadets to their third straight team championship.
"I was having a lot of trouble keeping with Cade," Compton said. "But I just forced myself to stay right behind him because I knew that downhill, I needed that to have a chance."
He hung back with Hill over a relatively slow first mile while West Valley's Hudson Meloy opened up a decent gap on the lead pack, something Compton said he expected. Shortly after the 2-mile mark Compton and Hill surged past Meloy and Davis senior Josh Whitney, turning it into a two-man race.
Compton finished second at both CBBN regular season meets, first behind Davis senior Josh Whitney at Sunnyside's South Hill Park and then last week behind Hill at Walla Walla Point Park in Wenatchee. But he also beat Whitney and Hill twice this fall, including when Compton ran a personal-best 14:51 for the 5K at the Nike Hole in the Wall Invitational.
Orcutt's win gave her four in seven races this season, including both CBBN regular season meets and the Melon Fest in Hermiston, Ore. She'll look to improve on an 18th place finish in Pasco, where last year she led the race at the end of the first straightaway before just missing the podium in 18th place.
"I had an infection and I was sleeping really bad every night and we didn't know until after state," Orcutt said. "It was just a week of really bad sleep and being sick."
She believes that experience will help her race smarter and give something close to her best next Saturday, when she hopes to finish in the top five. The rest of the Rams will join her, since they finished second behind Moses Lake.
The Mavericks boys squad beat Eisenhower by three points in the last league meet, so Cadets coach Robert Price knew it would be another close race for the district title. Wolfgang Nelson finished sixth while Maxwell Prescott and Casey Smith-Apperson also placed inside the top ten to give Eisenhower a 14-point advantage over Moses Lake.
"Everyone had to do their job, including Kian," Price said. "It was good. They ran tough. Kian ran super hard."
Price said he's enjoyed seeing the efforts put in by all of his runners, who benefit from seeing an elite talent like Compton every day at practice. Ike will be trying to improve on its 16th and 14th place finishes the past two seasons at Sun Willows Golf Course next Saturday.
Whitney hung on for third place in his first race since Oct. 10, when he ran a 15:55 at the Nike Hole in the Wall Invitational despite a back injury. Meloy took fourth, earning the sophomore his second straight trip to state.
Eisenhower's Zophie Hopkins easily qualified for her fourth consecutive 4A state meet by placing sixth, tied for her highest finish ever at the district meet. Price said the senior did well to stay in control and run a smart race.
"She got some girls today that she hasn't been able to get all season and I think part of that's the course," Price said. "Some of those girls, you can't get out fast in this first mile."
Orcutt pushed hard to reach the first mile mark in 5:45, about 16 seconds faster than anyone else. She said she wanted to test her training and open up a big gap, then settle in and have fun the rest of the way.
Senior Zoey Moon gave West Valley a solid fifth runner in her second race back from an ankle injury, which kept her from even coming to practice for part of the season. Orcutt said it felt great to have Moon's leadership back on the course, and they're looking forward to seeing if they can match or beat their ninth-place finish from the state meet a year ago.
BOYS
Team scores: Eisenhower 41, Moses Lake 55, West Valley 65, Davis 103, Eastmont 121, Sunnyside 148, Wenatchee 190.
Local state qualifiers: 1, Kian Compton (Ike) 15:25; 3, Josh Whitney (D) 15:51; 4, Hudson Meloy (WV) 15:55; 6, Wolfgang Nelson (Ike); 7, Caedmon Brandon (D); 9, Maxwell Prescott (Ike); 10, Casey Smith-Apperson (Ike); 11, Landon Moon (WV) 16:40; 13, Ian Naught (WV) 16:41; 15, Errol Strom (Ike) 16:45; 18, Britten Butler (WV) 17:06; 21, Henry Johnson (Ike) 17:21; 32, Da'Zaylan Mc'Kinnie (Ike) 18:27.
GIRLS
Team scores: Moses Lake 26, West Valley 44, Eastmont 69, Sunnyside 111, Wenatchee 127, Davis 173.
Local state qualifiers: 1, Callie Orcutt (WV); 6, Zophie Hopkins (Ike) 19:27; 8, Vera Attig (WV) 19:37; 10, Evelyn Jordan (WV) 19:54; 14, Alivia Brandt (WV) 20:17; 15, Zoey Moon (WV) 20:25; 17, Arianna Rios (WV) 20:56; 22, Kayla Gill (WV) 21:29.
